messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: R/qtl version 1.08-56
parts:
I found a slight but deadly bug in the scanqtl() function in the
recently released R/qtl 1.08-55. Thus, I've released a new version,
1.08-56, at the R/qtl website. The Windows and Mac binaries should be
available within a few days.

As always, I'd appreciate hearing any suggestions or comments or
complaints.

Karl Broman
kbr...@biostat.wisc.edu

messages.author: 7409d4321b2ec671
messages.subject: Re: R/qtl version 1.08-56
parts:
Dear Karl,

I’m enjoying to play with 1.08-56. Its functions are very well
organized and easy to use!
By the way, I found the different result of scantwo between 1.07-12
and 1.08-56 using the same data set. Did you update scantwo as well
when you released 1.08-56?
I’m wondering because one of my main QTL-QTL interaction was
disappeared in the result of scantwo 1.08-56.
Unfortunately, I discarded version 1.07-12. If its possible, can I
have version 1.07-12? So I can recheck whether something wrong with my
data.

I love rqtl and hope rqtl will stay around for long-long time!
Thank you.

Best,
Masato

You can download version 1.07-12 at the following:

source: http://www.rqtl.org/download/old/qtl_1.07-12.tar.gz
windows: http://www.rqtl.org/download/old/qtl_1.07-12.zip

I don't believe there were any fundamental changes in scantwo in
version 1.08-56; it's hard to say what is happening without more
detail on the results and the data.

karl

messages.author: 7409d4321b2ec671
messages.subject: Re: R/qtl version 1.08-56
parts:
Dear Karl,

Thank you for your info!
And, I must apologize that I misunderstood the reason I got the
different result of scantwo between 1.07-12 and 1.08-56. That was not
the change in 1.08-56.
I run sim.geno for each of analyses (in 1.07-12 and 1.08-56,
n.draws=100 each) and run scantwo with the imputation method usually.
When I run scantwo in 1.08-56 with n.draws=128, I could get almost
same result with a meaningful QTL-QTL interaction as I got once.
But if I run scantwo with n.draws=100, I couldn't get that interaction
in the result neither in 1.08-56 nor 1.07-12.
my cross is F2 cross of fresh water fish,
384 of F2 were genotyped and only 125 of 384 of them were phenotyped.
I guess the low number of phenotyped F2 may cause this inconsistency.
I appreciate it if you would suggest the fair number of multiple
imputation times (= n.draws) for my case or in general.

plotLodProfile function saves my time a lot!

Thank you very much!
Masato

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Re: R/qtl version 1.08-56
parts:
Analysis with scantwo will consider only the phenotyped individuals.

If there is appreciable missing marker genotype data or the markers
are not very dense, you may need a larger number of imputations (n.draws
in sim.geno). If you run sim.geno and then scantwo a second time and
get rather different results, you should probably increase the number of
imputations.

karl
